questions.q: What is the main message of the passage?
options: Industry and labour, especially among humble inventors, built England's greatness
Natural talent matters more than effort in producing great inventors
Steam engines were first conceived by English mechanics in the 19th century
England's greatness was won by its aristocracy and its laws
questions.explain: It praises industry and credits men of humble rank for most great inventions.

questions.q: Who is called 'the laborious, patient, never-tiring' figure among steam-engine pioneers?
options: Savary, the military engineer
Newcomen, the Dartmouth blacksmith
Cawley, the Dartmouth glazier
James Watt, the instrument maker
questions.explain: It names James Watt as towering above the other pioneers.

questions.q: Who first promulgated the idea of the steam-engine centuries earlier?
options: Hero of Alexandria
Hugh Miller
Mr. Edgeworth
Cawley
questions.explain: The idea promulgated by Hero of Alexandria was never lost.

questions.q: What was Mr. Edgeworth's view on intellectual differences?
options: They stem mainly from differences in social rank and wealth
They depend chiefly on schooling in the classics and mathematics
They depend more on early attention habits than on natural power gaps
They are mostly inherited and cannot be changed by training
questions.explain: He held that difference depends more on early cultivation of the habit of attention.

questions.q: What does the author suggest about Watt's success?
options: He simply knew more than anyone else living in his time
Wealthy patrons funded his work and secured his success
Diligence and disciplined skill, not superior knowledge, made him great
He was the most naturally gifted mind of his generation
questions.explain: Many men knew more than Watt, but none laboured as assiduously.
